artifacts.summary: Writer-script precedent analysis (events-append.sh/system-defect-record.sh/orchestrate-record-decision.sh), re-measured orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh threading point and orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh/orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh call sites, and recommended MIRROR/LEAVE/RETIRE verdicts for the six existing issue surfaces including corroborated-dead reflection field.

memory_candidates.content: scripts/orchestrate-record-decision.sh is the per-task-file (not global-file) append-one-validated-entry precedent in this codebase: it resolves TASK_DIR from a bare --task N via scripts/lib/task-lookup-lib.sh's task_lookup_entry/task_lookup_dir (archive-aware), uses a dedicated per-task lock file ($TASK_DIR/.decisions.lock, distinct from task-lock.sh's mutex), and documents a read-merge-validate-mv write under flock for a JSON array document. Distinct from events-append.sh/system-defect-record.sh, which append JSONL lines to a GLOBAL file. Any new per-task structured log should pick the write mechanics (array-mv vs. JSONL-append) based on whether the target file is a bare array or an append-only line log, not just copy whichever precedent is named first.

The state.json 'reflection' field is corroborated dead by two independent methods: (1) grep across every live postflight script (skill-base.sh, update-task-status.sh, orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh, state-write.sh) finds zero writers; (2) its sole writer, scripts/orchestrator-postflight.sh, is itself already documented in-repo (skill-base.sh:991) as having no live callers. context/reference/state-management-schema.md's prose describing a live producer for this field is aspirational/stale, not a description of working code — a reminder that schema-reference docs in this codebase can describe intended-but-undeployed wiring, not just current behavior, so a 'field exists in the schema doc' finding needs a grep-for-live-writer follow-up before being trusted.

orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh's per-dispatch prompt-section line ranges drift across unrelated tasks that land first: a dispatch-authored 'measured ~417-558' estimate was already ~20 lines stale by the time the dependent task's own research ran, from two already-completed, file-footprint-serializing dependency tasks (one touching this same build-dispatch script, one touching the sibling postflight script). Any task description citing line ranges in these two files should be treated as a hint to re-measure, never as ground truth, even when the citing task explicitly says RE-MEASURE — the drift is real and fast, not a hypothetical caution.
